speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me today. To better understand your neck swelling, can you tell me how long it has been present and if it has changed in size?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Neck.

Given your history of colon cancer and a persistent, painless, progressive neck mass over two months, I need to confirm the nature of this lesion. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, ESR, and CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck Ultrasound or CT Neck with contrast.
